newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Family of Bre-X geologist wants body exhumed.
newsitem.headline: Family of Bre-X geologist wants body exhumed.

text.p: The family of the Filipino geologist who helped discover what had been touted as the world's biggest gold find this century said on Tuesday they were unsure the body they buried was his and said they wanted it exhumed and re-examined.

Michael de Guzman, chief geologist of Bre-X Minerals Ltd, died in an apparent suicide in March when he fell from a helicopter in Indonesia. It was later revealed that the gold he had discovered was almost worthless.
The badly damaged body was flown to the Philippines where his family buried him.
But his brother Jojo de Guzman said they now had doubts if the body they buried was that of his brother.
The doubts were raised after the family compared the body's fingerprints with those on an old identity card belonging to de Guzman.
"(The fingerprints) do not seem to match," Jojo de Guzman said as he showed two enlarged copies of fingerprints, one taken from the body and the other from an identity card.
Jojo de Guzman had earlier said he had not seen the face since it was badly damaged but had believed the corpse was his brother by looking at the body structure.
"Personally I believe it was Michael's. I can almost recognise the body frame, the facial features...it seemed like Michael," he said on Tuesday.
Jojo de Guzman said his family was traumatised by reports his brother had been sighted in various countries.
Even after he was buried last April 4, there were "ridiculous reports" that he had been seen in Argentina, Singapore and even in Indonesia, he said.
"We want everything laid to rest... The desire of the family is to have a DNA test to put everything in order," he added.
De Guzman was said to have helped find in the jungles of Kalimantan, Indonesia, an ore body that contained $25 billion worth of gold.
Bre-X's disclosure of the find sent its stock soaring as people invested millions of dollars in the company.

The stock began to plunge after de Guzman's mysterious death. Independent tests by another laboratory later said the find was almost worthless. The ore samples from the Busang find had been tampered with before being sent to the laboratory, they said.
Bre-X is now facing a spate of lawsuits.
The de Guzmans' lawyer, William Chua, said the family had asked the Philippine National Bureau of Investigation to check the fingerprints again.
Indonesian authories said Michael de Guzman committed suicide but his family has said it doubted he would take his own life.
